subject: Request: custom per-token rate & step-down commit for Aurora AI
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@aurora.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing for large usage profile (hosted API)

Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Aurora is excited about Redwood's latency profile and keyed caching. We ran a quick model usage forecast (attached) and are estimating roughly 200–300M generated tokens/month in year one, with a projected ramp to ~600M by Q3 next year.

Given that profile, our procurement leads have asked if Redwood can offer a custom per-token rate or a step-down commit tiering structure (rather than strict list-rate). We have competitive terms on the table from another provider and would like to understand what flexibility you have on per-token pricing for a 12–18 month commit.

Specific asks: 
- Can you provide a committed tier structure with step-down per-token pricing at 50M, 150M, 300M thresholds?
- Any one-time onboarding credits or usage credits for the first 90 days?
- High level billing model (monthly invoice vs. prepaid commit draws)?

I've attached our usage forecast and a short one-pager from procurement. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Samir Khan
VP Product & Ops, Aurora AI
[sent from Aurora HQ]

[attachment: Aurora_usage_forecast.xlsx]

Also copied are a couple of items that will speed approvals: SOW template and billing contact if procurement wants a single PO route. I'll get an internal recommendation back by EOD Monday.

Subject: Internal: Aurora AI — request for custom tiering & discount approval (AUR-2026-Q4-7892)

Team —

Aurora (cc Samir) has submitted a usage forecast that implies a large hosted API commitment (200–300M gen tokens/mo Y1; ramp to 600M). They are asking for a step-down per-token tier and potential credits for onboarding.

Proposed structure (initial ask from AE):
- 12-month term, monthly billing against a committed monthly minimum (we can discuss upfront prepay as an option)
- Step-down per-token price windows at: 0–50M, 50–150M, 150–300M, >300M
- Target list discount: they are expecting ~25–30% off published per-token list based on competitor term; they asked us to match.

Requesting pricing guidance:
1) Recommend tiered per-token rates (please include both list and proposed discounted rates).
2) Approval limits — what % off list can pricings approve directly? Where do we need escalation to VP/Revenue?
3) Any standard onboarding/credit playbook we should offer for first 90 days?

Attachments: Aurora_usage_forecast.xlsx, SOW_draft_v0.1.pdf (draft SOW I shared earlier).

Timing: Aurora wants a commercial term sheet this week; pushing for decision timeline. If this requires a rate-card exception beyond standard thresholds, flag so I can prep for a VP signoff.

Thanks — jasmine

[attachment: SOW_draft_v0.1.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Aurora AI — request for custom tiering & discount approval (AUR-2026-Q4-7892)

Jasmine — thanks for the context and the forecast. A few pragmatic suggestions below.

1) Approach: Commit + tiered per-token is the right model. It preserves predictability and gives Aurora upside as they scale. We should avoid unlimited overage buckets without >=30% premium on overage to discourage gaming.

2) Recommended tier table (example, per generated million tokens):
   - 0–50M: $6.00 / M tokens (list) — recommended offer $5.40 (10% off)
   - 50–150M: $5.25 / M (list) — recommended offer $4.20 (20% off)
   - 150–300M: $4.50 / M (list) — recommended offer $3.15 (30% off)
   - >300M: $4.00 / M (list) — recommend escalation for this band (we can offer up to 35% off with VP approval)

3) Approval glossary: Pricing team can approve up to 20% off list for any given band. Discounts >20% across a material band require VP signoff (Marissa). Anything >30% requires CFO notification for revenue recognition and margin review.

4) Onboarding credits: We typically offer a one-time ingestion/POC credit up to $25k for strategic logos tied to a 12-month commit; >$25k needs Sales Ops approval and finance signoff.

5) Billing model: prefer monthly invoiced against committed monthly minimum with a quarterly true-up. Prepay is acceptable if the customer requests it for cash flow reasons — in that case structure as a draw-down credit with non-refundable clauses for early termination.

If you want to propose the 25% across-the-board discount Aurora is asking for, we should position it as: 25% first-year introductory across the first two bands with the deeper discounts triggered by actual usage verified after 60 days. That would be a good middle ground to bring to Marissa for a quick sign-off.

cc: Vivek to confirm engineering/ops ramp capacity and collect any SLA asks.

—Sean
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Aurora AI — request for custom tiering & discount approval (AUR-2026-Q4-7892)

Thanks team — reviewed Sean's recommended table and Aurora's forecast. Given the size and strategic fit (large Gen-AI customer, potential expand into Dedicated later), I approve a one-year commercial exception as follows: 

Approved commercial summary (subject to SOW + CFO signoff):
- Term: 12 months with quarterly usage reviews.
- Commit: 12-month minimum equivalent to 150M generated tokens/mo (billed monthly).
- Pricing (first 12 months):
   - 0–50M: $5.40 / M tokens
   - 50–150M: $4.20 / M tokens
   - 150–300M: $3.15 / M tokens
   - >300M: $3.00 / M tokens (overflow requires explicit addendum and CFO/DCC approval)
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied as invoice credit in month 1.
- Conditions: ELA-style overage guardrails; 60-day usage verification to lock tiers; standard Redwood SLA language with escalation clauses.

This is effectively a ~25% blended concession vs. list for Y1 and is a conditional exception to the published rate card. Please prepare a commercial term sheet and SOW reflecting the above and route to Legal + Finance for sign-off (I will approve the exception). Once Legal confirms, send the DocuSign link to Samir and procurement.

Jasmine — please own the customer comms and ensure procurement has the billing contact and PO path. Vivek — confirm we can commit to the requested throughput and flag any engineering constraints.

Marissa Cole
VP Revenue, Redwood Inference
